PROVENANCE — python/tests/fixtures/faultdecode_golden.json
==========================================================

Re-recorded on : 2026-08-10
Recorded from  : the SHIPPING Python CLI, `tan 0.5.2-rc1.dev0`
                 (`python/tan/version.py::TAN_VERSION`) — for TWO decode_cases
                 only. Every other value in the file is still the original
                 alp-sdk recording and was not touched.
Issue          : tan-cli#616 (defect A)
Branch         : fix/616-faultdecode-escalation-and-negative-cfsr (off dev @ 1813e46)
Interpreter    : Python 3.12.3, lane-private venv, `tan` resolved from this worktree.

What this file is, and what changed about that
----------------------------------------------
The file was frozen from alp-sdk's `scripts/alp_cli/faultdecode.py`, of which
`tan/core/faultdecode.py` is a port. It carries two sections:

  * `bit_tables`   — every (register, bit, name, meaning) quadruple.
                     UNCHANGED by tan-cli#616. The register-level facts are
                     ARM architectural definitions and are not what diverged.
  * `decode_cases` — 102 swept cases (a single-bit sweep over cfsr/hfsr/dfsr
                     plus a handful of composed/realistic words), each with
                     `report_json` and `render_human`.

Two of the 102 were re-recorded. Both differ in `root_cause` and in NOTHING
else — measured before writing, by diffing `report_json` with `root_cause`
removed and finding it equal:

    cfsr=0x00000020 hfsr=0x0 dfsr=0x0  (MLSPERR alone)
      - "MLSPERR set (MMFSR): MemManage fault during lazy floating-point
         state preservation."
      + "MemManage fault while lazily preserving the floating-point context
         -- the MPU forbids the deferred push of the FP registers into the
         space the exception frame reserved for them (wrong region
         permissions, or a stack that has overflowed out of its region)."

    cfsr=0x00002000 hfsr=0x0 dfsr=0x0  (LSPERR alone)
      - "LSPERR set (BFSR): Bus fault during lazy floating-point state
         preservation."
      + "Bus fault while lazily preserving the floating-point context -- the
         deferred push of the FP registers into the space the exception frame
         reserved for them hit a faulting address, so that stack memory is bad
         or absent (a corrupted or overflowed stack pointer). Check SP/PSPLIM
         and that the stack fits the larger FP-extended exception frame."

`render_human` moved for the same two cases and for the same reason: it prints
`root_cause` verbatim under "Most likely cause:". The "Set flags:" block of
both is byte-identical, LSPERR/MLSPERR included — the bit tables did not move.

How it was re-recorded
----------------------
Not by hand. The two values were produced by calling the shipping
`tan.core.faultdecode.decode()` / `report_to_json()` / `render_human()` with
each case's OWN recorded `cfsr`/`hfsr`/`dfsr`/`bfar`/`mmfar` inputs — i.e. the
same three calls `tests/core/test_faultdecode.py::test_decode_matches_the_
frozen_golden` makes, so the recording cannot drift from the comparison. Cases
whose output was unchanged were left byte-for-byte alone; the resulting diff is
4 lines.

Why the change was correct, and why it was a DIVERGENCE (CLOSED below)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
tan-cli#616 defect A: `HFSR.FORCED` (bit 30) is the ESCALATION MECHANISM — a
configurable fault escalated because it could not be taken — not the fault.
The fault is in CFSR. At the time, upstream's `_root_cause` ladder had no
branch for LSPERR (BFSR bit 13) or MLSPERR (MMFSR bit 5), the only two CFSR
cause bits it had never given one, so those two words fell past every branch
and landed on `FORCED`. This is no longer true as of `dad5b35a` (see CLOSED,
below) — recorded here only as the history that motivated the divergence:

    $ tan faultdecode --cfsr 0x2000 --hfsr 0x40000000
      Most likely cause:
        Forced HardFault -- a configurable fault escalated but its own status
        bits are clear; ...

— which is not merely the least actionable half of what the registers say, it
is FALSE: LSPERR is set, so its own status bits are demonstrably not clear.

tan now (a) gives LSPERR/MLSPERR real root-cause branches and (b) makes
`FORCED` the headline only when CFSR names no cause at all. This was a
deliberate, maintainer-decided divergence, reserved for exactly this decision
in tan-cli#539 and taken in tan-cli#616; `tan/core/faultdecode.py::_root_cause`'s
docstring recorded it at the source, and `tests/core/test_faultdecode.py::test_
decode_diverges_from_the_sdk_original_only_where_tan_cli_616_declares` policed
it against a live alp-sdk checkout — a mismatch OUTSIDE the declared classes
still failed.

CLOSED, 2026-08-12: alp-sdk `dad5b35a` ("fix(faultdecode): lead with the
escalated fault, not the escalation (#1389)", folding #1358) ported both (a)
and (b) into `scripts/alp_cli/faultdecode.py` verbatim -- upstream followed, as
this file originally asked. `tan/core/faultdecode.py::_root_cause`'s docstring
now records the closure instead of an open divergence, and the policing test
was renamed to `test_decode_matches_the_sdk_original_including_the_classes_
tan_cli_616_used_to_diverge_on`: it asserts byte-equality again, including on
these two classes, while still proving (by tan's own answer, not the oracle's)
that the sweep keeps reaching the words that used to diverge.

Note what this file could NOT have caught, and still cannot
-----------------------------------------------------------
`decode_cases` is a SINGLE-BIT sweep plus a few composed words. It contains no
`CFSR-cause + HFSR.FORCED` combination at all, which is why the FORCED-shadows-
the-cause half of defect A left every one of the 102 cases green and had to be
found by hand. The FORCED guard is therefore pinned by named unit tests in
`tests/core/test_faultdecode.py`, not by growing this fixture: these 102 rows
are upstream's answers, and adding tan-only rows would blur what the file is.

Why re-recording is an ordinary change now
------------------------------------------
It was not always. tan-cli#539 reserved both halves of #616 because
`contract/envelopes` goldens also held the FROZEN Rust v0.4.1 oracle to the
same bytes, so changing the output reddened `crates/tan-cli/tests/contract.rs`
on every platform. tan-cli#269 deleted `crates/` (`2883cdf`) and tan-cli#594
re-recorded the affected goldens against the shipping Python CLI. There is no
second gate left to disagree with this fixture. (Independently: `contract/
envelopes/` has no `faultdecode` case at all — checked, 17 case directories,
none of them this verb — so no envelope golden moved for #616.)
